name: Program in Neural Computation (PNC) PhD

english.note: Non-native English speakers must provide TOEFL or DET; IELTS accepted but TOEFL/DET preferred. Tests normally expire after two years. Prior US-degree holders may submit older scores. Tests still required for non-native applicants with non-US undergraduate degrees, including UK/Canada. No numeric cutoff stated.

applicationFee.note: No fee to submit a PhD application; no waiver needed.

documents: English unofficial PDF transcripts from every college/university attended, even without a degree
Research statement, 1–2 pages: education, research roles/results, proposed interests and faculty fit
requirements.note: GRE optional; applications with and without scores fully reviewed. No GPA cutoff. Faculty contact encouraged to establish availability; identify potential faculty in statement/application. If generative AI is used, briefly disclose how at the end of the essay; content must reflect your own voice. Joint PNC programs with ML/Robotics/Statistics are petitioned only after PNC acceptance, not direct applications. Letters: At least two from faculty or recent employers; electronic submission only. Submit by December 1 despite another FAQ allowing a longer period for recommenders.

funding.note: All NI PhD candidates funded regardless of immigration status: full tuition for at least five years with satisfactory progress, annually set living stipend, 100% individual SHIP premium, $500/year travel and one-time computer purchase. Dental and vision cost extra.

summary: PhD training in neural computation through Carnegie Mellon’s Neuroscience Institute.
detailsNote: December 1 is a recurring deadline without an entry year. Fall 2027 and a single admission model are not confirmed by these pages.
